text:
ali: quick sync. saw unexpected duplicate credits reported by accounting for a very short window during a regional failover test. not a large footprint but want to get protocol hardened.

omar: is this the manifest/CAS work we discussed?

ali: similar class but different trigger. timeline: 1) region A loses connectivity to control-plane 2) local consumers in region A keep running and emitting using cached manifest epoch 3) control-plane in region B issues emergency reassignment and increments epoch in manifest 4) when connectivity restores, region A continues with stale epoch emissions -> duplicates.

sret: cross-region are gnarly. we need to define "safe read staleness" for consumers and a conservative lease TTL. maybe require consumers to renew manifest lease periodically; if they can't contact KV, they must pause emitting unless they have a recent lease.

becky: ops concern: pausing emits during control-plane outage could cause data loss or gaps for high-throughput tenants. maybe emit into a local buffer with a tombstone header that marks "tentative-epoch" and ship only when we can verify lease. but then reconciler becomes heavier.

omar: hybrid again: consumers can continue producing event stream to an in-region write-ahead topic but must not send to billing-sink until they refresh manifest or are within lease window. billing-sink will reject tentative-epoch headers. reconciler will drain the write-ahead topic when manifest sync resumes.

ali: suggests defining two modes: active-mode (connected to control plane, attach canonical epoch) and buffer-mode (no control-plane, attach tentative-epoch + local-instance-id). buffer-mode writes to local durable topic partition only. reconciler later merges and assigns epoch deterministically based on manifest history and dedupe.

sret: security note: tentative-epoch events must be marked and signed so we can verify origin and avoid replay attacks. add source-instance signature header.

becky: ops retention: we can keep write-ahead topic for up to 24 hours; reconciler SLA should be to drain within 6 hours after control-plane restores. this caps disk usage.

omar: implementationally, extend manifest with lease_expiry and last_renewed_by fields. consumers periodically refresh lease via lightweight heartbeat. on heartbeat failure, consumer enters buffer-mode.

ops-bot: created incident stub INC-2026-002 for cross-region handoff dupe test and assigned to ali and becky.

ali: next steps: 1) define lease TTLs and heartbeat cadence (sret + ali), 2) prototype local write-ahead + tentative-epoch headers (omar), 3) reconciler draining rules and safety checks (becky). I'll collate into RFC addendum.

becky: also suggest adding a deploy-time flag to enable tentative-mode only for lower-risk tenants during failover testing.

ali: good idea. thanks all.
